info.title: freehire API
info.description:
## Base URL

All endpoints are served under `https://freehire.me/api/v1`. The API is read-first and open: the job, search, facet, and company endpoints need no authentication and may be called cross-origin.

Authenticated endpoints accept either the browser session cookie (set by sign-in, same-origin) or a personal API key sent as a Bearer token — see the authentication model below. Keys are created in your account, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys), not through this API.

## Response envelope

Single items are wrapped as `{ "data": ... }`. Collections add pagination metadata: `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "total", "limit", "offset" } }`. Errors are `{ "error": "message" }` with a matching HTTP status.

```json
{ "data": { "...": "single item" } }

{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 4213, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }

{ "error": "job not found" }
```

## Pagination

List and search endpoints page with `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset` (default 0). `meta.total` reports the total matching the current filters, so you can compute the number of pages.

Pagination is bounded on **every** list endpoint: `offset + limit` may not exceed 10000 (`pagination too deep` → 400). This is deep-paging protection, not a cap on the reported total — use filters to narrow rather than paging that far.

The bound is a refusal rather than a clamp, deliberately: a clamped page would answer 200 carrying rows you did not ask for, and a client walking pages would loop over the same page forever without being able to tell. A 400 means "there is no such page", which is the truth.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes: 400 (bad request / invalid value), 401 (missing or invalid credentials), 403 (authenticated but not allowed, e.g. a non-moderator), 404 (no such job, company, or owned resource), 429 (request limit exceeded), and 503 (service temporarily unavailable). Application errors use `{ "error": ... }`. nginx rate-limit rejections can return a non-JSON body; see API plans below.

## API plans

The public read endpoints answer without a key for personal and non-commercial use. Showing the postings in a product you offer to others needs an [API plan](https://freehire.me/jobs-api), under the [data licence](https://freehire.me/terms#data-licence).

Send a full-access key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or use the OAuth access token of a signed-in MCP or CLI connection.

The API plan allows 1,200 requests per 60-second window. The Data plan allows 6,000. Neither paid API plan has a daily request cap. The account shares one budget across its full-access API keys and OAuth connections, including public REST reads and agent search. A browser session cookie does not select the paid API rate.

The limit counts HTTP requests, not returned listings or unique vacancies. A page containing 100 listings costs one request. Re-fetching the same page or vacancy costs another request, including when the data has not changed. There is no separate cooldown for refreshing a vacancy.

Pagination returns 20 listings by default and up to 100 with `limit=100`. Requests carrying `offset` or `company_slug` also pass through separate per-IP nginx limits of 2 requests per second each, including paid requests. The `offset` limit allows a burst of 50 excess requests; the `company_slug` limit allows 30. A request carrying both parameters draws on both limits. For sustained pagination or company-filtered reads, keep the combined traffic from one IP within the applicable 2-request-per-second limit.

The gateway returns `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until reset). A window starts with its first request. Exceeding a request limit returns HTTP 429. Gateway rejections include `Retry-After` in seconds; nginx rejections can omit these headers and return a non-JSON body. Pause for `Retry-After` when present; otherwise back off before retrying.

## Authentication model

Browser clients authenticate with an `HttpOnly` session cookie set on sign-in (same-origin; the SPA cannot read it). Non-browser clients use a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Endpoints marked “Session or API key” accept either; endpoints marked “Session only” (saved searches, subscriptions) accept only the cookie, so a leaked key cannot manage credentials. “Moderator” endpoints additionally require the moderator role.

## What is not here

This reference covers every endpoint you can call. A handful are deliberately left out because calling them directly is meaningless: the Gmail and calendar consent redirects (`/me/gmail/connect`, `/me/calendar/connect`, and their callbacks), which only a browser can complete; the Telegram bot webhook; the browser-tool websocket relay; the sitemap-cursor helpers behind `/sitemap.xml`; and the `/og/*.png` social-preview cards, which render an image rather than answer with JSON.

Managing API keys (`POST`, `GET` and `DELETE` on `/me/api-keys`) is not documented here, because no API client can call it. Those endpoints accept only the browser session cookie, and additionally require a freshly proven identity — a password re-entry or a sign-in-provider check — that a script has no way to supply. Create and revoke keys in your account instead, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys); the plaintext token is shown exactly once, at creation, so store it then.

The `/jobs/{slug}/fit` endpoints are pre-rename aliases of `/jobs/{slug}/match-analysis` and hit the same handlers. They still work, so existing clients do not break — use the match-analysis paths in new code.

Most of this API is also a CLI. If you are writing an agent rather than an integration, `freehire` covers the same surface with less ceremony — search, tracking, the inbox and CV tailoring — over one API key.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Public, unauthenticated reads. Jobs are returned in one wire shape (addressed by `public_slug`, never an internal id) shared by the list, detail, company, and search responses. Closed postings are excluded from lists and search and served only by the detail endpoint.

tags.name: Fit
tags.description: Personalized signals computed against the caller’s profile or stored CV. All accept the session cookie or an API key. The skill-match endpoint is deterministic (no LLM); the match-analysis endpoints run the LLM chain and draw on your daily allowance. All take the same facet filter params as search where they narrow a market or candidate set.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Public reads. A company detail also returns a page of its open jobs.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text job search with the shared filter vocabulary, facet counts, similar jobs and the reference data behind search.

tags.name: Company feedback
tags.description: Signed-in users leave a 1–5 star rating plus category and text about a company, shown under their site-wide pseudonymous persona (never a user id). Reads are public; writes are cookie-only. A reader can report a specific review, and a moderator can hide it.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Register/login set the session cookie and return the user. Logout clears it. `me` resolves the caller (cookie or API key). OAuth sign-in is a redirect flow.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description: Per-user tracking, addressed by the job slug. Writes are idempotent. The response is the interaction record for that job.

tags.name: Assistant
tags.description: The same agent the web app and browser extension chat with, over HTTP: create a conversation, then post messages to it. All routes accept the session cookie or an API key (`autopilot` is cookie-only — see below) and act on a session you own; someone else’s session id answers `404`, same as one that never existed. Turns run one at a time per session — a message sent while one is already running queues rather than running alongside it. `preset` selects which conversation this is: `chat` (default), `profile` (the experience interviewer), `browse` (a browsing session held from the extension’s side panel), `interview` (a mock-interview rehearsal), `debrief` (after a real one) or `apply` (the conversation about one automatic application) — the last three must name the vacancy via `?job=<slug>`, an application you already hold. An application holds one `apply` conversation: asking again returns it with `200` instead of creating a second. A `tailor` session cannot be created here; it is minted by the CV tailoring bootstrap, which knows the CV and vacancy to bind it to.

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description: Any signed-in user can submit a vacancy for moderation and read their own queue. The review actions are moderator-only; approval mints a live job.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Any signed-in user can flag a problem with a live vacancy. Review actions are moderator-only; resolving may soft-close the reported job.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Votes on jobs and companies, and ghost reports: one person states they applied to a posting and were never answered, feeding the ghost-signal evidence used elsewhere in the API (see the `reality` field on a job). Nothing here reaches a moderator and nothing here closes the job directly.

tags.name: Résumé
tags.description: Your career profile and stored CV, session-only (a browser feature, like saved searches). The profile is a singleton keyed by your session — no id in the path. The verdict and ATS report are read-only sub-resources computed from the profile and CV; résumé storage degrades to `501` when object storage is unconfigured.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: Aggregate market intelligence, all public and all unauthenticated. Every figure is served from a precomputed rollup rather than counted live, and nothing here exposes a record-level field or a user identifier — these are counts over the catalogue, not a way to read it.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Browser conveniences, session-only. A saved search stores a canonical filter query string; a subscription turns one into a recurring digest (Telegram, email, or your own webhook). Each operation is owner-scoped — a non-owned id is a 404.

tags.name: Contributions
tags.description: Turning a URL in the wild into something freehire knows about. One intake sequence serves every surface — the website, the bot, the extension and the CLI — deliberately, so a pasted link gets the same answer everywhere.

tags.name: Community
tags.description: The lighter per-user surfaces: a vote on a job or company, the account-level notification rule (gates the saved-job apply reminder and both lifecycle nudges), and the public discussion threads. Votes and notification settings take a key; posting to a thread is browser-owned.

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Two sides of the same marketplace: an employee offers to refer into the company they work at (proof required, moderated), and a candidate asks one of that company's approved referrers for an intro. A candidate never sees who the referrer is, and a referrer sees the candidate's CV only through a short-lived view. Moderation of offers is moderator-gated.

tags.name: Talent Network
tags.description: A public, anonymised catalogue of candidates who opted into being found. Membership is a single toggle on `users`, distinct from `user_profiles`; a member is addressed by a minted handle, never by their account id or username. Every string a public response carries is a value a dictionary resolved, a number or a date — never text copied from a CV — so no name, employer, institution or free-text field appears anywhere in it.

tags.name: CV
tags.description: Your CVs, and the tailoring flow that reframes one toward a single vacancy. Authoring is browser-owned — create, update and delete are session-only — while reading a CV, patching it, and rendering the PDF also accept an API key, because that is the half a tailoring agent drives. Every CV is owner-scoped: an id you do not own is a 404, not a 403.

tags.name: Experience
tags.description: The durable record a CV is built from: employments, and the evidence atoms under them. Every atom carries who asserted it — you, or a model that inferred it — and only your own assertions may be written into a CV. Reading accepts an API key; editing is session-only.

tags.name: Mail
tags.description: Your job mail, and the link between a message and the application it belongs to. Mail arrives three ways: a connected Gmail account, the hosted freehire address, or a batch your own client pushed. Only the first two are classified by freehire — pushed mail is yours to triage, which is what makes that tier free. Everything here takes a full-scope API key, so a harness can drive the whole surface; the Gmail consent redirect is the one exception and stays browser-only.

get.summary: Search with full descriptions, for programmatic/agent consumers.
get.description:
Same text query and facet filters as `/jobs/search`, but each result carries the
`description` in full (verbatim from the database) instead of the truncated index
preview. Use `description_format` to choose how it is rendered.

Plus every filter in the "Filtering jobs" section.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text query over `title`, `company`, `description`, and `location`. Plain words
use the default engine matching: the first words are required and trailing ones are
dropped when too few postings match, so word order can change the result. Operators:
quotes (`"systems engineer"`) require every quoted word in any order (not a
contiguous phrase); `-word` excludes; uppercase `OR` between words matches any
alternative (at most 5, merged and deduplicated); `title:` at the start of an
alternative matches it in the title only, e.g.
`title:"product owner" -junior OR title:produktchef`. Narrow the fields of the other
alternatives with `q_fields`. Exact-phrase matching is not offered, and default
relevance order does not reliably rank a contiguous match above a scattered-token
one. (e.g. `golang`)

parameters.name: q_fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of `title,company,description,location` to restrict `q` to,
e.g. `title`. A name outside that set drops the whole parameter (reported in
`meta.ignored_params`) rather than partially applying. (e.g. `title`)

parameters.name: description_format
parameters.description: `text` or `markdown`; anything else leaves the stored HTML.

post.summary: Start a new conversation.
post.description:
For shortlisting the current jobs list, pass search_query (the complete serialized
query; an empty string is valid) and a client-generated request_id UUID. Only chat
sessions accept this binding. Reusing the UUID with the same owner and canonical query
returns the same session; changing its query returns 409. Unknown search parameters
return 400 at creation. A condition that cannot be enforced when a search runs (for
example hide_seen without a readable history) fails that search instead, and the
assistant reports it rather than widening the search. Search-bound responses include
search_context: { query, brief }; the original query is immutable and the selection
brief is local to the conversation.

parameters.description:
Public slug of an application you hold. Required for `interview`/`debrief`/`apply`,
ignored otherwise. (e.g. `senior-go-engineer-acme-1a2b`)

post.summary: Buy a CV editing session another ceiling’s worth of turns.
post.description:
A CV editing session is bounded by a turn ceiling as well as by the daily session
allowance, and a turn past the ceiling is a `402` naming the session. This spends
another of the day’s CV editing sessions to raise it (no body), and is idempotent under
a double click — two calls in flight buy one ceiling, not two. `409` on any preset
other than a CV editing session: a chat is bounded by the daily assistant allowance,
and a day cannot be topped up. `402` when there is no session left to spend, with the
same body every refusal carries.

server: take the returned `value` to `calls_url` (this deployment’s own realtime
gateway, not api.openai.com directly) to negotiate the WebRTC call. `501` when voice
mode is not configured.

post.description:

forward in context. Returns `204 No Content`.

post.summary: Re-read your own store subscription now.
post.description:
For a mobile client that has just completed an App Store or Google Play purchase. The
purchase finishes on the device before the provider’s webhook reaches us, and if that
delivery is lost the provider stops retrying after 80 minutes — so without this route a
paid subscriber can be left looking at a paywall. It names nobody: the account is the
session’s, and a user id in the request is ignored. Absent entirely where the store
provider is unconfigured. `status` is `synced` when the plan was written, or
`no_subscription` when RevenueCat holds nothing for this account; a 503 means the
provider could not be reached and the hourly reconciler will finish the job.

narrows the set. Continuous numeric facets are returned as `stats` (min/max), not

get.summary: Resolve a posting URL to a catalogue slug.
get.description:
Answers `{"data": null}` when the posting cannot be identified, rather than 404 — "we
do not carry this" is a normal answer here. Used by the extension to tell whether the
page you are on is a job we already have. A miss also carries `meta.ats_board`: true
when the URL sits on an ATS board freehire knows how to crawl, so a client can tell a
posting worth adding from an arbitrary page.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The posting's URL in the wild. (e.g. `https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/123`)

post.summary: Hand freehire a link: import the posting, and the board behind it.
post.description:
Five outcomes in one shape, distinguished by status: **200 found** — the catalogue
already carries the vacancy. Either the URL itself is stored (nothing is fetched or
written), or the page turned out to be a second copy of a posting we already carry
under another source, in which case the answer names the one we had; **201 tracked** —
we crawl that board already and the posting just had not landed, so it was imported
now; **201 imported** — imported, and its board queued for onboarding; **201 review** —
imported, but its careers site names no board we can crawl, so the link went to manual
triage; **202 queued** — nothing could read the page, so the link went to manual
triage. `company_slug` is returned whenever the catalogue already carries the employer,
through any source — independent of what became of the board. A URL that is not http(s)
is a 422.

get.summary: Full-text + faceted search over open jobs.
get.description:
Combine free-text `q` with any of the filter params below. Repeated facet params are
ORed; add `<param>_mode=and` to require all, or `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude.
Without `q`, results default to newest first; with `q`, to relevance. A param no filter
reads is ignored rather than refused, and listed in `meta.ignored_params` — check it,
since a dropped filter otherwise looks like a broad result.

Plus every filter in the "Filtering jobs" section.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text query over `title`, `company`, `description`, and `location`. Plain words
use the default engine matching: the first words are required and trailing ones are
dropped when too few postings match, so word order can change the result. Operators:
quotes (`"systems engineer"`) require every quoted word in any order (not a
contiguous phrase); `-word` excludes; uppercase `OR` between words matches any
alternative (at most 5, merged and deduplicated); `title:` at the start of an
alternative matches it in the title only, e.g.
`title:"product owner" -junior OR title:produktchef`. Narrow the fields of the other
alternatives with `q_fields`. Exact-phrase matching is not offered, and default
relevance order does not reliably rank a contiguous match above a scattered-token
one. (e.g. `golang`)

parameters.name: q_fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of `title,company,description,location` to restrict `q` to,
e.g. `title`. A name outside that set drops the whole parameter (reported in
`meta.ignored_params`) rather than partially applying. (e.g. `title`)

parameters.name: hide_seen
parameters.description:
`true` leaves out the postings the signed-in caller has already opened (the 1000 most
recently viewed, saved, applied to or hidden), inside the search, so `meta.total` and
paging stay accurate. A per-person preference, not a filter: a saved search ignores
it. Without a session or API key it is not applied and is listed in
`meta.ignored_params`. (e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: hide_applied_companies
parameters.description:
`true` excludes every posting of employers represented in the newest 1,000
applications made by the signed-in caller. Employers represented only by older
applications can remain in results. Applied inside the search, so `meta.total` and
paging describe what is left. A per-person preference, not a filter: a saved search
carrying it narrows nothing. Without a session or API key, or with a value that is
not a boolean, the search runs unhidden and the param is reported in
`meta.ignored_params`. (e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: min_skill_match
parameters.description:
Keeps only postings whose skills your profile covers by at least this percent
(1–100), across the whole ranking. Applies only with `sort=match`, to a signed-in
caller with profile skills; the read stops once no later posting can qualify or at a
depth bound, and then `meta.total` is a minimum with
`meta.total_is_lower_bound: true`. A per-person preference: a saved search ignores

seed.description: Pre-fills the CV from the stored résumé structure.

CvPlanRefusal.description: A plan refusal: the sentence, the allowance it does not include and the upgrade link.

agent_session_id.description: The assistant conversation bound to a tailored CV; empty when none.

autopilot_report.description: The last unattended run's account of itself; absent when no run has happened.

tracer_links_enabled.description: The candidate's consent for this CV's links to be traced.

CvRecord.description: One CV: its document and the state around it.

base_cv_id.description: The base to copy; absent means the default base.

analysis.description: The cached fit analysis, or null.

cold_start_running.description: True exactly when this call created the tailored CV.

CvTailored.description: A tailored CV in the re-open list.

distinct_visitors.description: Absent when the deployment has no visitor salt.

CvTracerLink.description: One traced link as the owner reads it.

DerivedLocation.description: Where the CV says the caller IS, as the location dictionary resolved it. Read-only.

request_count.description: How many people have asked for this term.

tailored.description: The CV tailored for this vacancy, null when none.

DirectApplyCVOptions.description: What the signed-in candidate can send.

resume.description:
Send the CV file uploaded to your profile. Exactly one of `resume` and `cv_id`. (e.g.
`true`)

cv_id.description:
The CV you tailored for THIS vacancy (`cvs.tailored.id` from the form). Any other CV

answers.description:
Question id → answer; a yes/no answer is `"true"` or `"false"`, a list answer one of
its options. (e.g. `{"q1":"true"}`)

note.description: Up to 2000 characters to the employer. (e.g. `Happy to talk this week.`)

DirectApplyRequest.description: Names the CV to send: `resume: true` for the uploaded one, or `cv_id`, exactly one.

EmailPrefs.description: The preference page's state: the address mail goes to and the three switches.

EmailPrefsSearch.description: One email digest subscription the switches govern.

EmailPrefsTokenUpdate.description:
The token-opened patch. The token rides in the body so it never reaches an access
log. Optional on the wire because a missing token must be refused exactly like a
forged one (404), not with a 400 that tells the two apart.

EmailPrefsUpdate.description: A patch: an absent switch keeps its stored value. Searches can only be turned off.

EmbeddingProgress.description: Every figure is null until it has been measured.

email_confirmed.description: Whether the claimant still owes the mailed code or is waiting on a moderator.

EmployerAccount.description: A company account. `user_id` is the address the moderator and admin actions take.

email_confirmed.description: Whether the claimant still owes the mailed code or is waiting on a moderator.

EmployerCompany.description: The account plus its company's curated profile; an unset profile field is left out.

EmployerCompanyPatch.description: An absent or null field is kept; `industries` replaces the whole curated set, even as `[]`.

EmployerQuestion.description: `type` is "text", "boolean" or "select"; `options` are a select's choices.

EmployerVacancyCreate.description: `title` is required, and `url` too unless `apply_mode` is "freehire".

EmployerVacancyPatch.description: An absent or null field is kept.

viewed_since.description: The first day `viewed` covers, YYYY-MM-DD; null when nothing is rolled up yet.

cluster_id.description: Shared id of a soft-duplicate group (its first member), when the list clustered this atom.

ExperienceAtom.description: One piece of evidence, at the grain of a CV bullet. The three flags below are computed at read time.

ExperienceBank.description: The places with their achievements, and the achievements that belong to no place.

link.description: Portfolio URL, typically on a project.

ExperienceEmployment.description: One place where evidence was produced. A job carries `company`; a project carries its title as `name`.

link.description: Portfolio URL, typically on a project.

ExperienceProvenance.description:
How the bank came to hold an achievement. Only the first three are the candidate
speaking and may be written into a CV; `agent_inferred` is the assistant's own reading.

facets.description: Facet param, then value, then count. Every covered facet is present.

FitAnalysedJob.description: One analysed job in the caller's list.

allowance.description: Where the caller stands on the fit allowance today; null when it cannot be read.

FitAnalysis.description:
The fit analysis for one job. `has_cv` is false when the caller has no stored CV;
`stale` marks a cached analysis whose CV or job changed since; `analysis` is null when
none is cached or the model is unconfigured. The allowances ride on reads only and are
absent when they cannot be read.

FitMatchTextRequest.description: A job posting scraped off any page.

upgrade_url.description: Absent for a fair-use refusal and for a caller already on the top plan.

FitRefusal.description: The 402 a spent or missing fit allowance answers with.

GeoSet.description: A geographic reach: regions and/or ISO country codes. Empty means worldwide.

applied_on.description: The date the caller applied, YYYY-MM-DD.

GmailStatus.description:
Whether Gmail is connected. `email` and `status` are sent only when a connection row
exists; `available` says whether the connect flow is configured on this deployment.

total.description: Cumulative members as of that day.

HealthStatus.description: The derived health verdict for a provider, the fleet or the site.

IgnoredMeta.description: The meta of a single-item answer, sent only to carry a warning.

IgnoredParam.description:
A query param the endpoint did not read: unknown, or known but unreadable
(`min_years=lots`). Either way the answer is wider than the caller asked for.

job.description: The job in the shared wire shape.

stage_suggestion.description: The stage the newest classified message implies; absent when there is nothing to offer.

auto_apply.description: The caller's live auto-apply attempt for this job; absent when none exists.

InboxApplicationDetail.description: The job, the caller's interaction with it, the linked mail and the history.

InboxEmail.description: One message with its body. The internal raw-MIME pointer is not exposed.

InboxLinkTarget.description: Names the application: a catalogue job's slug. Required, 400 when empty.

InboxLinking.description: The classification and link overlay every message carries; each is absent when empty.

InboxMessage.description: One row of the listing. `body_text` is sent only when the listing asked for bodies.

hidden.description: How many messages the default filter suppressed.

signal.description: One value from the vocabulary above. (e.g. `interview_invitation`)

slug.description: Link the message to this application at the same time.

InboxTriage.description: The verdict an agent records for one message. Left-out fields read as empty.

Interaction.description:
The caller's interaction with one job. Every timestamp, the stage and the notes are null
until the job is viewed, saved, applied to, dismissed or tracked.

total.description: The whole closure's open size, even when the list is a capped page.

JobCopy.description: One per-city opening folded under a canonical job.

JobCreate.description: The moderator create body. url, title and company are required, and the service refuses a request without them.

JobDescriptionSource.description: Exactly one of `job_slug`, `url` and `text`; anything else is a 400.

ats_board.description: Whether the URL sits on an ATS board freehire knows how to crawl.

JobFindResult.description: `data` is null when the posting cannot be identified, and then `meta` says whether the board is crawlable.

JobFoundPosting.description: The posting a page URL is, when the catalogue carries it.

notified.description: Only on a decision: whether the reporter was actually told.

JobReportReason.description: The closed reason vocabulary (internal/engage/report validReasons and the CHECK on job_reports).

ignored_params.description: Absent when every param was read.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` counts only what was read, not the whole match.

JobUpdate.description: The moderator edit body: a field left out or null is unchanged.

ignored_params.description: Absent when every param was read.

total_is_lower_bound.description: True when `total` counts only what was read, not the whole match.

ListMeta.description: A page of a filtered list, with what the filter dropped.

LocationPreferences.description:
Where and how the caller wants to work, as it is stored and echoed back: normalised,
with `remote`, `base` and `relocation` always present and empty lists left out. Every
member is optional on a save, and an entirely empty block clears it.

MailFollowUpDraft.description: A chase the candidate sends themselves; `recipient` is absent when nobody ever replied.

MailRecalledEmail.description: One message the recall sweep proposes. `id` is 0 for a message the search found.

MailRecalledPick.description: The message the caller picked out of a sweep. Required, 400 when empty.

week_start.description: The current ISO week's Monday, YYYY-MM-DD.

MentorProfileSuggestions.description: A prefill for the mentor-profile form, from what the account already knows.

MentorshipBooking.description: One session as a party to it sees it; seeker_email only for the mentor.

MentorshipCalendarStatus.description: `booked`: a confirmed session; `busy`: a synced interval from the mentor's calendar; `free`: offered to seekers; `closed`: outside the stated availability.

MentorshipDirectoryMeta.description: `ignored_params` lists the query params the directory did not read.

seniority.description: Absent when the mentor left it unset.

MentorshipMentor.description: A mentor as the PUBLIC sees them: the directory card and the profile read are one shape.

seniority.description: Absent when the mentor left it unset.

meeting_url.description: Absent while the mentor has not set one.

MentorshipOwnMentor.description: A mentor as their owner sees them: the moderated shape plus the room and the session parameters.

seniority.description: Absent when the mentor left it unset.

MentorshipPendingMentor.description: A pending profile in the moderation queue.

MentorshipProfileStatus.description: The moderation status of a profile. `withdrawn` is a mentor who has left; the row survives it.

ids.description: Exactly two achievement ids; anything else is a 400.

jobs.description: The stored snapshot of a multi-job digest; left out for every other kind.

NotificationDigestJob.description: One job of a multi-job digest, as recorded at delivery (notify.SnapshotJob).

NotificationKind.description:
What a `user_notifications` row can be about. The column is free text; these are the kinds
the engines write (notify, reminder, nudge, buddy, messaging, auto-apply), plus
`auto_apply_tailor_ready`, which only historical rows carry.

channels.description:
Delivery channels: `email`, `telegram`, `push`. Adding `push` needs a device the
mobile app has registered (409 otherwise).

NotificationSettingsUpdate.description: Every field is read as its zero value when left out. Times are `HH:MM`.

PageMeta.description: Where a page sits in the whole list.

PendingCompanyRelationStatus.description: `approved` marks a merge whose job move stopped part-way; approving again resumes it.

PeriodDate.description: A year, with a month when the CV gives one.

PlanAllowance.description: Usage against a limit for one metered feature today.

amount_cents.description: The smallest currency unit, as the payment provider stores it.

default.description: The price a new subscriber is sold unless they choose another.

PlanSource.description: Where a paid plan was bought.

pro_until.description: When the paid plan lapses, absent on the free plan.

pro_source.description: Where the plan was bought. Absent on the free plan.

PlanTier.description: The tiers a caller can be on.

limit.description: The daily ceiling; with `unlimited`, the fair-use guard behind it.

PlanTierAllowance.description: What one tier allows for one feature in a UTC day.

enforced.description: The features whose ceiling refuses today.

url.description: The job posting URL to parse.

Problem.description:
Every refusal, whatever its status: `{"error": msg}`. `code` is set only where a
client branches on the reason (the auth flows).

count.description: How many people have reported this kind for the company.

ProcessReport.description: What a person reported about a company's hiring process.

ProcessReportKind.description: What a candidate can report about a company's hiring (vocab.CompanyProcessReportKindValues).

location_preferences.description:
What the caller asserted, shaped like LocationPreferences, sent exactly as stored;
null when they set none.

derived_location.description: What was derived from their CV; null when there is no current structured CV.

cv.description:
The contact-free CV, shaped like ProfileCV, sent exactly as the CV store writes it;
null when no current structure exists.

ProfileCV.description: The caller's CV without contacts: what they have done.

ProfileExperience.description: One work-history entry of the contact-free CV.

job_languages.description:
Preferred vacancy languages as two-letter codes (max 200); empty or omitted means any
language. (e.g. `["en","ru"]`)

location_preferences.description: Shaped like LocationPreferences; null or absent keeps none.

token.description:
The Expo push token minted by the device. (e.g.
`ExponentPushToken[xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx]`)

PushTokenTestResult.description: What a self-test send did per registered device.

RecentThread.description: A feed row: the thread plus the subject's display names, empty when the subject no longer exists.

ReferralCvKind.description: `original` attaches the uploaded CV; `built` one tailored in freehire.

approve.description: True approves the referrer; false rejects the offer.

ReferralIncomingRequest.description: What a referrer sees: the seeker's chosen contact and CV, never their user id.

job_slug.description: Names the vacancy; an unknown slug is a 404. Wins over `job_id`.

cv_kind.description: Which CV to attach: `original` (your uploaded one) or `built`.

cv_id.description:
The built CV, when `cv_kind` is `built`: one you tailored for that opening, or — with
no opening — for any opening at the company (see `cv-options`). Any other CV answers
422.

note.description: A short message to the referrer.

ReferralSeekerRequest.description: A seeker's own request: the target and status, no referrer identity.

block_domain.description: Also blocks the URL's host and rejects every other pending submission on it.

Relocation.description: The willingness to move. Open with empty targets means anywhere.

company.description: The company's fresh counters, set only on the answer to a write.

ReportedCompanyFeedback.description: A review with what a moderator triages by.

url.description: The job page the caller is on; anything not http(s) is a 422.

surface.description: Where the request came from (`extension`, `cli`, …), for the contribution record.

public_slug.description: The catalogue job; null while it is still queued.

ResolvedJobPage.description: Where a job page ended up.

ResolvedJobStatus.description:
What became of the board behind a job page: `found` (the catalogue already carried the
posting), `tracked` (imported, and the board is already crawled), `imported` (imported,
and the board queued for onboarding), `review` (imported, but no crawlable board could be
named) or `queued` (nothing could read the page, so the link went to manual triage).

skills.description: Required and at most 100 once blanks are dropped; anything else is a 400.

ResumeCoverageRequest.description: The skill list a coverage reading scores against the market.

sample_size.description: Only when a single role was named.

skills.description: Only when a single role was named; an empty list is a real answer.

coverage.description: The signed-in caller's own standing against `skills`; shaped like a job match.

skills_geography_scoped.description: Present, and false, only for a single role.

quantiles.description: The salary at every 5th percentile from 5 to 95 (19 values); empty until the rollup has computed them.

breakdown.description: "seniority" when every seniority's bands are returned.

SavedSearch.description: A named filter snapshot. `query` is the canonical search query string the SPA replays.

query.description: Empty is the valid "show all" snapshot.

SavedSearchCreate.description: An empty name is refused with a 400, like an out-of-range one.

SavedSearchList.description: The saved searches, most recently updated first.

SavedSearchUpdate.description: A partial update: an absent or null field is kept; an empty query is a real "show all".

status.description: suggested, confirmed or cancelled. A cancelled meeting is served.

ScheduledInterview.description: One arranged meeting. Unlike an event it can move or be called off.

authorized_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the candidate may work in.

privacy_consent.description: A standing agreement to an employer form's privacy terms; false asks each time.

ScreeningAnswers.description: Answers an application form asks for, saved once and reused. Each field is optional.

authorized_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the candidate may work in.

privacy_consent.description: A standing agreement to an employer form's privacy terms; false asks each time.

clear.description: Field names to clear. An unknown name is a 400.

text.description: The description of the search; refused over the length limit.

previous.description: The result being refined, echoed back from a prior answer.

SilenceState.description: Where an application sits against the silence thresholds of its stage (internal/job/silence).

error_rate.description: Fraction of 5xx responses over the trailing `window_minutes`, from the process's own traffic.

pool_pressure.description: Fraction of the database pool held at once, 0..1. Reported, never judged: it says what the error rate cannot, that requests are unable to start.

SiteHealth.description: The site's own verdict, independent of the ingest fleet's `overall`.

change_pct.description: Percent change from the first to the latest week; null without two weeks to compare.

SkillPulse.description: How demand for one of the caller's skills moved.

adapter.description: Whether the source is a crawl adapter at all.

jobs.description: Null until a snapshot has been taken for this source.

health.description: Null when no board health record exists.

browsable.description: Null when the search index could not be measured.

StageSuggestion.description: An offer to move the application to the stage its newest classified message implies.

job_slug.description: The minted vacancy's slug; on an approved submission in the caller's own list only.

Submission.description: A submission as the API shows it.

existing_job_slug.description: Set, with every other field empty, when the catalogue already carries the vacancy.

SubmissionPrefill.description: What could be parsed from the URL. Empty when it is not recognised.

SubmissionRequest.description: A vacancy to submit. url, title and company are required; the service refuses a body without them with a 400.

Subscription.description: One alert on a saved search. `saved_search_name` is sent on the list only.

jobs.description: How many open jobs the suggestion finds.

slug.description: The dictionary slug, when the part is one.

SuggestionPart.description: One recognised piece of the query: a dictionary term, or text still being typed.

helpful.description: Whether the conversation helped. A later vote replaces an earlier one.

biggest_challenges.description:
Any of `recruiter_contact`, `job_fit`, `remote_flexible`, `working_abroad`,
`visa_sponsorship`, `technical_interviews`, `english`, `first_job`, `just_starting`,
`other`. `just_starting` stands alone. Replaces the stored list. (e.g.
`["technical_interviews"]`)

biggest_challenge_note.description: Kept only while `other` is among the challenges.

current_income_amount.description: What you earn today, in the currency and period below. (e.g. `5000`)

SurveyResponses.description: The onboarding survey. Each field is optional.

TalentCard.description: The anonymised card: only what a dictionary can vouch for.

TalentEducation.description: One education entry: the degree level a dictionary resolved, and the year.

facets.description:
Facet name → value → member count. A count of -1 means the value is present but
held by too few members to say how many; 0 means nobody holds it.

stats.description: Ranged facets. The catalogue has none, so this is always empty.

TalentFacets.description: How many members stand behind each filter value.

timezone_region.description: The part of the zone before the slash; the `tz` filter reads it.

has_photo.description: Whether GET /talent/{handle}/photo has something to serve.

talent_handle.description: The handle in the member's public URL, once they have one.

listed.description: Whether the catalogue shows the member right now.

TalentNetworkVisibility.description: The caller's own place in the Talent Network.

TalentRole.description: One role of a work history, with everything nameable removed.

ThreadCursorMeta.description: `next_cursor` is set only when the page came back full; a partial page is the last.

ThreadStatus.description: A thread is open until a moderator closes it.

ThreadSubjectType.description: The author is the persona handle, "AI" for a system reply or "[deleted]" once the account is gone.

observed.description: The server's verdict on whether somebody other than the candidate set the date.

occurred_at.description: An instant, not a day: which day it falls on depends on the reader's clock.

TimelineEvent.description: One ledger event. An event happened and cannot change.

stage.description: Application stage from the vocabulary above. (e.g. `interview`)

TrackJob.description: At least one of the two is required. A field left out or null keeps the stored value.

id.description: Addresses the row: the posting's slug, or `a<id>` for an application whose posting is gone.

job.description: The job in the shared wire shape; null once the catalogue has removed the posting.

last_activity_at.description: The silence fields are null together on any row that is not awaiting a reply.

auto_apply_status.description: The status of this job's live auto-apply attempt; absent when it has none.

reply_rate.description: The reply-rate benchmark, only when it clears its sample gate.

TrackingPipeline.description: The application count and the count at each stage, zero included.

period.description: The plan day the figures cover, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.

Usage.description: Today's AI use on the account's own model credential. No money: the plan bounds use.

my_vote.description: The caller's own vote: 1 up, -1 down, 0 none.

names.description: Company names or slugs, one per entry. An empty list is refused with a 400.

unmatched.description: Entries that did not resolve to exactly one company, as typed.

max.description: How many companies one list may hold.

CookieSession.description: Browser session cookie set on sign-in (HttpOnly, same-origin).

PersonalApiKey.description: Personal API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
